title: Ignore the mailbox store so a cap never dirties the checkout
action: Add .bee/human-mailbox/ to .gitignore beside the other runtime stores. hm-2 wired an append at every cap, so a real bee cells finish now writes an untracked file into the checkout; unignored, every session dirties main and bee worktree merge refuses a dirty main.
acceptance: A cap that writes mailbox entries leaves git status clean; .bee/human-mailbox/ sits with the other ignored runtime stores.

trace.outcome: The mailbox store is git-ignored, so a cap that appends an entry no longer dirties the checkout or blocks a sibling session's merge
deviations: Found while verifying hm-2 rather than planned: hm-2 flagged the untracked store path as a next-phase question, but it dirties main on every cap today, which is the standoff that blocked two sessions for hours earlier in the session. Kind: hit an unforeseen obstacle.
trace.inline_reason: tiny lane, one .gitignore line, fully specified before execution; dispatch writes no state.workers row and bee state worker add refuses from a granted worktree (known P2)

report.outcome: The mailbox store is git-ignored so a cap no longer dirties the checkout
report.tests: git check-ignore -q on both .bee/human-mailbox/entries/probe.jsonl and a letter path — green (exit 0 for both) — the whole risk surface is whether both halves of the store are ignored
